chunks: And from him, from Ibn Faddal and Ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The kingdom of these men will not pass away until the people are slaughtered in Kufa on Friday. It is as if I am looking at heads falling between the mosque and the soap-sellers.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the slaughter in Kufa mentioned in the signs of Imam Mahdi's reappearance?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the transition of power as a precursor to the Mahdi’s reappearance, specifically linking the end of the 'Umayyad/Abbasid era rule to a decisive event in Kufa. The vivid imagery of heads falling between the mosque and the soap-sellers (*al-Sabun*) underscores the intensity of the conflict and the purification of the city, a theme often associated with the Battle of Karbala’s spiritual aftermath and the eventual establishment of justice. This event serves as a critical historical marker in Shia eschatology, emphasizing Kufa’s central role in the final triumph of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 448 - It is narrated from Fadhl from Ibn Faddal and Ibn Abi Najran from Hammad bin Isa from Ibrahim bin Umar Yamani from Abu Basir from Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) that he said:
“The kingdom of these men will not disappear until they slaughter people in Kufa on Friday. It is as if I was looking at heads falling between the Gate of al-Feel and (the place of) the soap-sellers.
